title: Right derived functor of an exact functor
statement:
Let $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and moreover
exact. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $RF\cong D(F)$, where $D(F)\colon
D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$ is the functor induced by applying $F$ termwise.

proof.text: Use the notation of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]: $Q_{\mathcal C}:K(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal C)$, $Q_{\mathcal D}:K(\mathcal D)\to D(\mathcal D)$, and $T=Q_{\mathcal D}\circ F_K$. Exactness of $F$ is precisely the additive, finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation required by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. That statement says that degreewise $F$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Hence $T$ inverts the quasi-isomorphisms of the homotopy category: represent such a morphism by a chain map $s$; its image under degreewise $F$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and its image under $Q_{\mathcal D}$ is invertible by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This uses no boundedness restriction and no resolution in $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, clauses (3)-(4) and proof; omitted universal-property details expanded using the cited localization node

proof.text: By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q_{\mathcal C}$ is a localization of $K(\mathcal C)$ at quasi-isomorphisms. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the functor $T$ of step 1, with target $D(\mathcal D)$. It supplies a functor $D(F):D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:D(F)\circ Q_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}T$. On a complex $K$, its component identifies $D(F)(Q_{\mathcal C}[K])$ with $Q_{\mathcal D}[F(K)]$, and on a chain map it identifies the image with the termwise image by naturality. Thus this is the functor induced by applying $F$ termwise, as in the statement. The same localization node makes any other factorization of $T$ uniquely isomorphic to this one compatibly with its comparison. Set $\epsilon=\varphi^{-1}:T\Rightarrow D(F)\circ Q_{\mathcal C}$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, clauses (3)-(4) and proof; omitted universal-property details expanded using the cited localization node

proof.text: We verify the derived universal property, rather than assuming that an invertible unit is universal. Fix $G:D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$ and $\beta:T\Rightarrow G\circ Q_{\mathcal C}$. The composite $\beta\circ\varphi$ goes from $D(F)\circ Q_{\mathcal C}$ to $G\circ Q_{\mathcal C}$. Both functors invert the quasi-isomorphisms since they factor through $Q_{\mathcal C}$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], with identity comparison isomorphisms, gives a unique $\gamma:D(F)\Rightarrow G$ such that $\gamma Q_{\mathcal C}=\beta\circ\varphi$. Equivalently $(\gamma Q_{\mathcal C})\circ\epsilon=\beta$. Conversely, this equation forces $\gamma Q_{\mathcal C}=\beta\circ\varphi$, so its lift is unique. Thus $\gamma\mapsto(\gamma Q_{\mathcal C})\circ\epsilon$ is bijective for every $G$. This is exactly the universal property specified in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor].

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, clauses (3)-(4) and proof; omitted universal-property details expanded using the cited localization node

proof.text: Let $(RF,\eta)$ be the chosen universal pair of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Its bijection applied to $\epsilon$ gives a unique $a:RF\Rightarrow D(F)$ with $(aQ_{\mathcal C})\circ\eta=\epsilon$. The bijection of step 3 applied to $\eta$ gives $b:D(F)\Rightarrow RF$ with $(bQ_{\mathcal C})\circ\epsilon=\eta$. Consequently $((ba)Q_{\mathcal C})\circ\eta=\eta$ and $((ab)Q_{\mathcal C})\circ\epsilon=\epsilon$. Injectivity of the respective bijections gives $ba=1_{RF}$ and $ab=1_{D(F)}$. Therefore $a$ is the asserted isomorphism $RF\cong D(F)$; its unique unit-compatible characterization makes it canonical. The uniqueness also identifies the comparison with the one for any other chosen localization factorization from step 2.
